turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Alright, quick vitals before the doctor. Blood pressure is 128 over 76, pulse 84, temp 98.4, oxygen sat 99 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Can we hurry this up? I'm wiped, and I've got a shift later.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hey. Sorry, err, this thing is still loading. Uh, what brings you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I found a lump. Left breast, in the shower.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): A lump. Sorry, which side again? I clicked into the wrong chart.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Left. I said left. It was Tuesday morning.
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You told me Sunday, hon. You came out of the shower Sunday and said you felt something.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): That was at my sister's, I was complaining about the water pressure. The lump was Tuesday. Four days ago. Don't mix him up.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right. Tuesday. My mistake.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Four days, left side. Any nipple discharge?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing coming out.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the lump hurt at all?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No it doesn't hurt. I would've said if it hurt.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cough or shortness of breath?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Breathing's fine.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): And your weight, have you lost any?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I don't know. My jeans are a little loose, but I skip lunch half the time and I don't even own a scale. Not really, I don't think.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mom had breast cancer. Diagnosed at fifty five.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, fifty five? Say that again, the screen jumped.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother. Fifty five. She's alright now, it was years back.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): And uh they told me my mamogram was borderline. About two years ago. Something about dense tissue, I was supposed to go back and I never did.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline mamogram, about two years ago, and you didn't go back. Alright, lie back for me.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): There's a firm lump in the upper outer left breast, about two centimeters, and it moves, edges feel smooth. No skin dimpling, and the nipple looks normal. I don't feel any nodes in the left armpit.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Two centimeters. Great. So do I just sit around waiting for a scan? I can't keep calling off work.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): I was gonna book a routine mammogram in about a month. Feels smooth and it moves, so that seemed reasonable.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A month? Her mother had cancer at fifty five, and she skipped the last callback.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yeah, you're right, I'm changing that. No waiting a month. Urgent referral to the breast clinic Thursday morning, with a mammogram and an ultrasound at that visit.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday. Do I have to fast or anything?
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): I booked you Thursday at 8:30. Radiology first, then the breast clinic. No deodorant and no powder on your chest, and you don't have to fast.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the pictures come back borderline, or they're unclear, then we do a biopsy. I'm not scheduling one today.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. I'm on low loestrin, one pill every morning. Does that screw up the pictures?
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep taking it, you don't need to stop for the pictures. Sorry, low loestrin, one every morning?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. One pill every morning. Can we wrap this up.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She takes vitamin D sometimes too. Not every day.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, whenever I remember. My head is killing me from that waiting room, but that's just today. Are we done?

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): This could be a fibroadenoma, but I can't rule out cancer until the imaging, especially with your mom's history. I'll see you back here in two weeks. If the lump grows quickly or the skin turns red, come in sooner.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
